study_material.title: Non-Verbal Reasoning - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Non-verbal reasoning tests pattern recognition without words: figure series, mirror and water images, paper folding, embedded figures, dice and painted cubes. Even in text form, the underlying logic (rotations, reflections, counting) can be mastered.
learning_objectives: Form mirror images and water images mentally
Solve dice problems using the opposite-faces rule
Count sub-cubes by painted faces in cut-cube problems
Reason about paper folding and punched holes

concepts.heading: 1. Rotations
concepts.body: A figure rotating 90 degrees clockwise per step returns to its start after 4 steps; 45 degrees per step needs 8. Track one distinctive element (an arrow tip, a dot) instead of the whole figure. Clockwise for the viewer is the standard convention.

concepts.heading: 2. Mirror and Water Images
concepts.body: Mirror image (vertical mirror): left and right swap - 'b' becomes 'd', 'AMBULANCE' is written reversed on ambulances. Water image (horizontal mirror below): top and bottom flip - 'M' resembles 'W'. Letters with vertical symmetry (A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y) look unchanged in a mirror.

concepts.heading: 3. Dice
concepts.body: On a standard die, opposite faces sum to 7: 1-6, 2-5, 3-4. From two views sharing a common face you can deduce the arrangement. Faces that appear together in one view can never be opposite.

concepts.heading: 4. Painted Cube
concepts.body: A cube painted outside then cut into n x n x n small cubes: corners (3 painted faces) = 8 always; edges (2 faces) = 12(n-2); faces (1 face) = 6(n-2)^2; inside (0 faces) = (n-2)^3. For n = 3: 8, 12, 6, 1.

concepts.heading: 5. Paper Folding and Punching
concepts.body: Each fold doubles the layers, so a hole punched through f folds appears 2^f times when unfolded, mirrored across each fold line. One fold + one punch = 2 holes; two folds + one punch = 4 holes.

formulas: Painted n-cube: 8 corners, 12(n-2) edges, 6(n-2)^2 faces, (n-2)^3 inner
shortcut_methods: Follow one marked element through rotations
For mirror images, check letters against the symmetric set
In dice problems, eliminate faces seen adjacent - they cannot be opposite
common_mistakes: Assuming faces seen together might be opposite
Forgetting the hidden inner cube in painted-cube counts
study_material.summary: Rotation cycles, reflection rules, the sum-to-7 dice rule and the painted-cube formulas cover the standard non-verbal questions.
quick_revision_notes: Mirror swaps left-right; water flips top-bottom

practice_questions.explanation: Water image flips top and bottom.

practice_questions.question: A figure rotates 45 degrees clockwise each step. After how many steps does it first return to its original position?
Two views of a die show 1 adjacent to 2, 3 and 4. Which number is opposite 1?
practice_questions.explanation: 1 cannot be opposite anything seen adjacent (2,3,4); on a standard die 1 is opposite 6.
